title: DRIFT: Joint Channel Estimation and Prediction Towards Pilotless 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
abstract: arXiv:2605.31065v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are expected to play a pivotal role in sixth-generation (6G) systems by enabling ubiquitous connectivity and massive communication. In this context, channel prediction emerges as a key technique to improve the spectrum utilization efficiency by limiting the pilot overhead. However, many proposed predictors based on artificial intelligence (AI) are characterized by high inference complexity, posing challenges to onboard implementation. In this paper, we address the challenge of designing accurate yet computationally efficient channel prediction techniques tailored to low Earth orbit (LEO) NTNs, where strict power constraints limit model complexity, to enable spectral efficiency gains. translated_title: DRIFT：面向无导频6G非地面网络的联合信道估计与预测
translated_abstract: 非地面网络（NTNs）预计将在第六代（6G）系统中发挥关键作用，通过实现无处不在的连接和大规模通信。在此背景下，信道预测成为一项关键技术，通过限制导频开销来提高频谱利用效率。然而，许多基于人工智能（AI）的预测器具有高推理复杂度，对星载实现构成挑战。在本文中，我们解决了为低地球轨道（LEO）NTNs设计准确且计算高效的信道预测技术的挑战，其中严格的功率约束限制了模型复杂度，以实现频谱效率增益。我们提出了一种在6G NTNs背景下的迭代联合信道估计与预测框架，该框架通过仅在初始时隙传输导频并依赖数据驱动来显著减少导频开销。
tldr: 本文提出了一种面向6G低轨非地面网络的迭代联合信道估计与预测框架，通过仅在初始时隙传输导频并利用数据驱动，显著降低导频开销，同时保持高准确性和计算效率，以应对星载功率约束。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an iterative joint channel estimation and prediction framework for 6G LEO non-terrestrial networks that significantly reduces pilot overhead by transmitting pilots only in the initial slot and relying on data-driven methods, while maintaining high accuracy and computational efficiency under strict power constraints.
